samples.summary: Google-only https install can silently issue session/refresh/state cookies without `Secure`/`__Host-`
samples.evidence: This delta removes `callbackScheme('GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL')` from `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:251-259). The PR itself makes a new deployment shape reachable: Google sign-in enabled (`GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL=https://…`), `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` unset (legal — GitHub falls back to the OAuth app's registered URL, see github.strategy.ts / oauth-providers.ts:32), `COOKIE_SECURE` unset, `NODE_ENV` not `production` (e.g. an install started with `pnpm start` or a compose file that never sets it). `isSecureCookie()` then returns false, so `sessionCookieName()`/`refreshCookieName()` (oauth-state.ts:89-95) drop the `__Host-` prefix and `setAuthCookies` (auth.controller.ts:544) / `oauthStateCookieOptions()` (oauth-state.ts:190) drop `Secure` on a genuinely https origin. Attack: an on-path attacker (or anything holding a sibling subdomain of the parent domain) triggers a plaintext `http://<host>/…` subresource and receives the session/refresh JWT, or plants `wafflebase_session=<attacker JWT>; Domain=<parent>` for session fixation and `wafflebase_oauth_state=<attacker secret>; Domain=<parent>` to defeat the double-submit login-CSRF check — exactly the properties the `__Host-` prefix comments at oauth-state.ts:26-47 and 66-84 say are load-bearing. The code comment (lines 230-234) acknowledges this shape and pushes it onto `COOKIE_SECURE=true`; confidence is low because it is a documented, misconfiguration-dependent trade-off rather than a default-configuration break, but the failure is silent and the impact is session theft.

samples.summary: The cleartext-origin warning is wired only to `GET /auth/github`, so a Google-only install never learns its cookies are insecure
samples.evidence: This delta's rationale (oauth-state.ts:214-234, github-auth.guard.ts:78-81) rests on `insecureProductionOrigin()` keeping the answer it had, and on operators being told when the origin reads as cleartext. `insecureProductionOrigin()` is consumed in exactly one place: `GitHubAuthGuard.warnIfInsecureOrigin()` (github-auth.guard.ts:209, 272-279), reached only from `GET /auth/github`. `GoogleAuthGuard.canActivate` (google-auth.guard.ts:38-46) calls `assertGoogleConfigured()` and `startWebOAuthLogin()` and nothing else, so on a deployment where users sign in with the Google button the warning never fires even under `NODE_ENV=production` with a plain-http origin — the session cookie goes out without `Secure` and no log line is ever emitted. Combined with the delta's decision that `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` no longer states the scheme, the one misconfiguration the design now depends on the operator noticing is the one with no detection on the Google path. Not a direct exploit, so minor; the defect is the missing signal, not a bypassed gate.
searchedFor: read AuthModule constructor/configure (auth.module.ts:89-117) for a boot-time warning

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described: isSecureCookie() (oauth-state.ts:251-260) resolves COOKIE_SECURE -> GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL scheme -> NODE_ENV==='production', with GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL deliberately excluded (comment at 214-234 names the exposed shape itself). That answer drives __Host- prefixing for session/refresh/state cookies (hostPrefixedCookieName:62-64, sessionCookieName/refreshCookieName:89-95) and the Secure flag on oauthStateCookieOptions:190, cliStateCookieOptions:141 and baseCookieOptions/setAuthCookies (auth.controller.ts:544, 501-521). The configuration is legal and reachable: GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL is optional (oauth-providers.ts:29-40; github-auth.guard.ts:66-72), so an https install configuring only Google, with COOKIE_SECURE unset and NODE_ENV not 'production', issues session/refresh/state cookies without Secure or __Host- on a real https origin. No guard closes this path: insecureProductionOrigin()/warnIfInsecureOrigin() (github-auth.guard.ts:97-103, 272-282) require NODE_ENV==='production', the exact branch excluded, and Dockerfile:121 only covers the shipped image, not a non-Docker/compose install behind a TLS-terminating proxy. cliLoginAvailable() (github-auth.guard.ts:83-85) fails closed only for the CLI flow, not for browser cookies. Impact is credential exposure over plaintext plus sibling-subdomain cookie tossing defeating the double-submit state check and enabling session fixation - in the auth/secrets lane. Being a documented, misconfiguration-dependent trade-off is not a named refutation ground, so the finding stands.
